finding.claim: The /invoice/<inv_id> route returns any invoice to any caller with no authentication or ownership check (IDOR / broken access control). The sibling /my/invoice route enforces owner checks, which shows the intended policy.
finding.source: inv_id URL path parameter from any unauthenticated or any-user HTTP request
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) returning the full invoice record, including the customer field

trace.note: Route registered with no auth decorator or before_request hook
INVOICES.get(inv_id) looks up the invoice by the attacker-supplied ID
Invoice returned without comparing inv['customer'] to g.user['id']

finding.guards_checked: There is no before_request or login_required in the file, and g.user is never referenced on this route. The only check is abort(404) for a missing ID. /my/invoice/<inv_id> at lines 16-17 has the owner check and this route lacks it. Only one file exists, so I could not check for an external auth middleware. If invoice IDs are unguessable, this limits enumeration but does not fix the missing authorization.

verdict.guard_found: none (only abort(404) for missing ID at invoices.py:9; no auth decorator or before_request in the only file)
verdict.reason: invoices.py:7-10 registers /invoice/<inv_id> and returns INVOICES.get(inv_id) via jsonify with no auth or owner comparison, whereas the sibling route at invoices.py:16-17 checks inv["customer"] against g.user["id"].
